cells.tense: You are at your work right now, and the adjustments are moving through you in real time.
cells.ask: Tell one person who watches you work what you weigh when you hold two things at once.
cells.core:
The balance is being worked, and it is being worked by you. Needs arrive together and you feel which one can wait and which one can't, then you move. That happens fast, in the middle of things, and it looks like nothing from outside. It is the whole job.

You are not settling for the middle. The thing you want most stays in the picture while you read the room, and neither gets quietly dropped to keep things calm. You hold your own pull, the other person's side, what the day can hold — and let them stay different from each other while you decide what each one gets today.
cells.sheetLine: You keep what you want in view while you read the room.
cells.verb: adjusting what you give each pull as they arrive together
cells.place: standing toward the light you are drawn to

cells.tense: You are out ahead of the disagreement, smoothing a version where nobody is upset yet.
cells.ask: Say one true thing that could cause a disagreement, then let it stand without fixing it.
cells.core:
Two people who want different things can stay in the room together with the difference still on the table, and both of them still there. The adjusting serves that. It is not supposed to erase the difference.

Right now it is spent on getting the disagreement over before anyone gets to have it. The version where no one is upset gets reached for first, so nothing is fully said. Surface kept even, distinctions dropped, and the distinctions were the point. What gets lost is contact with the person in front of you, who is being met by a smoothed version instead of by you.
cells.sheetLine: Kept even by holding the disagreement off the table.

cells.tense: The room came apart some time back and you have been living in the pieces since.
cells.ask: Tell one person close to you one thing you can't get back to, and let them hear it.
cells.core:
The steady version goes like this: one engagement ends and the next one starts, and something of you stays through both. What you want, what you're reading from the room, what you're carrying — those stay in touch with each other across the day, and the adjusting happens from that.

What is happening instead is that each thing takes the whole of you and leaves nothing for the next, so you begin what comes next from nothing and no center to arrive from. The adjusting isn't the part that's failing; the ground it would adjust from is missing. Trying harder to be even won't build it. One person close enough to hear where you actually are, not to fix it, is what gets you back on your feet.
cells.sheetLine: Entering what comes next from nothing, and the next too.

cells.tense: You are making calls all day and filing them under how it went.
cells.ask: Name one thing you do your own way, and tell someone how you learned it.
cells.core:
The steady version: someone adjusting as they go — adding a little here, holding back there — knows those were their calls. The way of doing things gets passed along, taught in their own words, kept because it is theirs to keep.

What is happening instead is that the adjusting runs all day and gets filed under circumstance. The situation managed itself, the right thing happened, nobody decided. The calls were made. Naming one of them — one thing you do your own way, and where you got it — puts the making back where it already was. It won't change what happened. It changes what you get to keep from it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that this person's life actually contains moments of holding several incompatible pulls at once while staying oriented by one star, for Balanced, and that the same holds at the other poles. A reader could reasonably say no, the opposite is true, I do collapse into every engagement and there is no cloth in my hands at all. The ask survives being wrong in all four cells because it only asks for a local act, not a verdict about how they live. The sentences that serve me more than them: 'the cloth in your hands' as a recurring image, and 'the wanting itself was the compass' — either could be removed and the cell would read cleaner.
